item.title: Where’s the strategy?
item.description: If the US has a strategy when it comes to the wars on Russia and Iran, it is not obvious. Instead of pursuing an end to hostilities in Ukraine, there is talk of using tactical nuclear weapons. Instead of honoring the MoU, Washington turns to more sanctions on Iran. These are strategies to continue war. CrossTalking with Dan Kovalik, Ethan Levins, and Alexandre Guerreiro.

item.title: CrossTalk Bullhorns: Ground invasion?
item.description: How many times does Trump want to lose the war on Iran? We will find out if a ground invasion is ordered – and it seems likely. Also, we are told Ukraine is winning. Then what explains the deepening internal divisions consuming the Kiev regime? CrossTalking with Mark Sleboda and George Szamuely.

item.title: Strange new world
item.description: The US-Israeli war on Iran is far from over. It is possible it may never really end. Nonetheless, the geopolitics of West Asia has experienced a fundamental shift. American military power has limits, and this has profound implications for the entire world. CrossTalking with Matthew Ehret, Ryan Milton, and Michael Rossi.

item.title: And so it goes…
item.description: The conflict in Ukraine and the war on Iran is reshaping the global order. The West, led by the US, refuses to accept the reality of multipolarity. This is exactly what these conflicts are about – the reshuffling of the geopolitical chessboard. CrossTalking with Dmitry Babich and Aleksandar Pavic.

item.title: War without purpose
item.description: The war is back on and this appears to be one of attrition. Trump and his supporters have never been interested in a negotiated end to the conflict. They still demand Iran’s surrender. That is not going to happen. Iran can say no. CrossTalking with Steve Jermy, Michael Scheuer, and Matteo Capasso.

item.title: Taco, again
item.description: It would seem that Trump can’t make up his mind. Continue the war he and Israel started with Iran, or pursue renewed negotiations? The problem is the US military does not have the means to continue the conflict and Iran is unlikely to accept any proposal from Trump. Iran has all the cards. CrossTalking with Dimitri Lascaris and David Swanson.
